title: Daisy
description: A puncture-capped daisy derivation is verified in the marked disk and available as an interactive substitution. The framed inner-boundary relation remains to be developed.

sections.Surface and conventions: A disk with marked points, treated as punctures. A twist about one marked point is trivial; this is not the framed-boundary daisy relation.
sections.Derivation: The four-point formula follows from two PC lantern substitutions and cancellation of a repeated two-point twist. The same argument gives a recursive n-point formula.
sections.Braid factorization: The under-going pair twists have explicit conjugating braid words, and the full disk Artin action checks the substitutions.
sections.Planar mapping class diagrams: The boundary-twist playground renders all four factors with the shared surface library.
sections.Standard mapping classes: The final four-factor product consists entirely of positive Dehn twists; no inverse twist remains after cancellation.
sections.Equivalences and transformations: Expand the leading three-point twist by the PC lantern to obtain the pairwise PC rose factorization.
sections.References: See the linked derivation and Margalit–McCammond, Geometric presentations for the pure braid group, Section 4.
